title: Safeguard Verification: Isobutane Pump Reinstated (Zero Energy Verification)

interruptions.title: Pump Recommissioning Interruption
interruptions.description: Field operator reaches by radio asking for permission to start the pump recommissioning.

objectives: Define what constitutes a safeguard and the requirements for verification.
Recognize when it is necessary to physically verify safeguards.
Demonstrate awareness and appropriate utilization of start work checks to align expectations and estimate time needed to verify safeguards before commencing work.
Develop strategies and use techniques to improve communication skills and facilitate better communication from others throughout planning, preparation, and execution.
Facilitate concise pre-job briefings with 2-way dialog so all team members are informed about job scope, potential hazards, and key steps for successful execution.

learner_prompt: You are the outside operator and permit approver-verifier. In each scene, state what you do and say, and why. Ask for missing information. Reference safeguards and procedures explicitly. Focus on verifying safeguards, confirming zero energy (including vent/bleeder verification), and using clear, closed-loop communication.

star_criteria.label: Verified zero energy
star_criteria.criteria: Award this star if the learner directs the team to open the bleeder valve or otherwise explicitly verifies zero energy through the bleeder.

roleplay_nodes.title: Outcome: Incident (Gap Missed, Flange Break)
roleplay_nodes.description: Work proceeds to flange break. Residual pressure/gas releases; local monitors alarm; workers evacuate. One crew member becomes ill and is transported offsite. Emergency response protocol initiated; no fatality.

role_play_persona.name: Tom
role_play_persona.objective: Get the crew safe and coordinate immediate actions with the verifier and control room.
initial_messages: Stop—stop! We’ve got a release! Back out—get upwind!
One of the guys is dizzy—getting him to fresh air. We need medical response now.

tasks.description: Confirm evacuation/accountability and initiate immediate controls aligned to site protocol (high level; not a quiz).
tasks.completion_criteria: Learner confirms evacuation/accountability, communicates immediate controls/coordination needs, and uses closed-loop communication.

initial_messages: Hey Brad here, I'm right at the pump. We've completed the isolation steps. Can you give me the go-ahead to start the pump recommissioning?

tasks.description: Refuse to approve start of the pump recommissioning without proper verification.

competency_rubric.name: Communication
competency_rubric.description: Develop and implement strategies to enhance communication skills, facilitate effective pre-job briefings, and ensure accurate dissemination of critical information. Listen to others and communicate effectively and in a manner that fosters open communication.

criteria: Listen actively without interrupting or distracting the speaker.
Check own understanding of others' communication (e.g., repeat, paraphrase or ask questions).
Present appropriate information in a clear and concise manner, both orally and in writing.
Take time to organize facts and ideas, incorporating relevant data, information and examples before communicating or presenting in a meeting.
Recognize structural or grammatical mistakes that obscure the meaning of a message.
Use techniques to improve communication, such as three-way communication, asking open-ended questions, and asking questions to clarify areas the FFL does not understand.
Elicit comments or feedback on what is discussed.
Encourage others to listen and contribute to dialogue, remaining open to new and different perspectives.
Openly and constructively discuss diverse perspectives that could lead to misunderstandings.
Communicate decisions or recommendations that could be perceived negatively, with sensitivity and tact.
Facilitate comprehensive pre-job briefings with two-way dialog to confirm that all team members are informed about the job scope, potential hazards, and key steps for successful execution.
Confirm the crew is aware of scope and critical steps of the work.

Develop strategies and use techniques to improve communication skills and facilitate better communication from others, fostering a collaborative and transparent work environment throughout planning, preparing, and delivery of work.
Provide positive feedback during discussion to encourage participants to continue.
Enable thorough discussion by giving equal attention to others' perspectives whether or not you agree with them, refraining from correcting others or completing their thoughts.
Respond to and discuss issues or questions in an understandable manner without being defensive.
Use varied communication systems, methodologies and strategies to promote dialogue and shared understanding.
Communicate complex issues clearly and credibly with widely varied audiences.
Anticipate reactions to messages and adapt communications accordingly.
Role model active listening, frequently paraphrasing the input of others to ensure understanding while recognizing nonverbal cues to get to the true meaning behind the words.
Use two-way communication to align opposing points of view with your position.
Critique the oral and written communication of subordinates and encourage them to develop these skills.
Develop a communications strategy for various audiences in order to achieve objectives, considering the optimal message to present, timing and forum of communication.

competency_rubric.name: Safeguard Verification
competency_rubric.description: Verify critical safeguards prior to high-consequence activities. Know, implement and ensure compliance with company safe work practices; recognize and report HSE-related noncompliance, incidents or concerns and ensure employees work safely at all times.

criteria: State what action you must take if you believe it is not safe to start or continue with a work activity.
List personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements for routine work.
Identify safety, lifesaving and emergency rescue equipment at your work location.
Define the term 'muster point'; describe how to identify a muster point and state the location of your designated muster point.
Describe the different types of audible and visible emergency alarms and the action required for each alarm.
Recognize safety sign color coding.
Name the types of work permits and the standard work permit attachments.
Define the term 'confined space'; identify company and site procedures relevant to working in a confined space.
State the procedure for reporting safety noncompliance; safety hazards; near misses, incidents and accidents.
Identify situations or locations where you may encounter extreme temperatures while working.
List the five steps involved in designing a 'Safe System of Work' (SSoW).
Use Preventing Serious Injury and Fatality Field Guide and Start Work Checks as reference.
Verify safeguards prior to work commencing.
Confirm critical safeguards when conditions change.
Select and wear appropriate PPE for nonroutine work and specific hazards.
Describe possible reasons why it may not be appropriate to use your designated muster point in an emergency; give the direction and route that should be taken to an alternate muster point.
Identify all safety signs used on the facilities.
Describe the purpose of a work permit; assist in the preparation of a work permit.
Identify common risks associated with working in a confined space and the steps that must be taken to mitigate risks associated with working in a confined space.
Recognize and report using the correct procedure safety noncompliance; safety hazards; near misses, incidents and accidents.
Identify common risks associated with working at height and steps that must be taken to mitigate risks associated with working at height.
Identify common risks associated with working in extreme temperatures and the steps that must be taken to mitigate risks associated with working in extreme temperatures.
Apply the SSoW process to work activities.
Define what constitutes a safeguard and requirements of verification.
Explain what a safeguard is and is not and provide examples of safeguards relevant to own work.
Describe what verification means and how it applies to own role.
Describe how to use stop work authority when a safeguard could not be verified.
Verify the Start Work Check is completed.
Reinforce and allocate the time to perform verification as designed.
Ensure that all personnel at your worksite know and comply with the site policy, procedures, rules and guidelines.
Identify competencies required for maintaining a healthy and safe work environment.
Ensure that all employees and contractors wear correct PPE, and that their PPE is complete and free from defects.
Ensure that appropriate safety, lifesaving and emergency rescue equipment is available at work location.
Verify that all personnel know the location of their designated muster point, the location of alternate muster points and the circumstances in which an alternate muster point should be used.
Ensure personnel respond correctly to emergency alarms; carry out emergency alarm drills and training.
Ensure appropriate safety signs are displayed where required.
Complete a work permit ensuring all requirements of the permit are met.
Ensure compliance with procedures, standards and guidelines for working in a confined space.

Investigate, evaluate and submit through proper channels corrective action or follow-up recommendation for safety noncompliance; the risk of actual and/or potential safety hazards and the actual or potential consequences of near misses, incidents and accidents.
Ensure compliance with procedures, standards and guidelines for working at height.
Ensure compliance with procedures, standards and guidelines for working in extreme temperatures.
Oversee work activities and ensure that they are carried out according to the SSoW process.
Demonstrate the awareness and utilization of start work checks to align with expectations and accurately estimate the time needed to thoroughly verify safeguards before commencing work.
Ensure that all employees have access to current site policy, procedures, rules and guidelines, and that all superseded documents are promptly removed.
Ensure that all personnel are competent in and comply with site HSE performance standards.
Ensure that there is an adequate supply of serviceable PPE and that damaged or time expired PPE is removed and disposed of correctly.
Routinely inspect all safety, lifesaving and emergency rescue equipment; ensure it is appropriate for the work location and serviceable.
Ensure HSE training needs are identified, and appropriate training is provided for all personnel; ensure that all personnel have appropriate and current safety training and certification.
Routinely inspect all safety signs; ensure they are appropriate for the work location and clearly visible.
Verify that permit requirements are met and it is safe to work.
Monitor and ensure proper investigation and close-out of all findings and recommendations for safety noncompliance; safety hazards; near misses, incidents and accidents.
